title: Saving a different Part Status asks to confirm first
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919), a role that has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Create & Edit' and 'Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-ASKFIRST-01) is tracked at {Location-A} and is active.
custom_steps:
1. On the Active tab search {Part-A} and click its row.
  2. Pick Part Status "Inactive".
  3. Click Save.
  4. Read the dialog that opens.
  5. Click "Cancel" in that dialog, then click Cancel in the part dialog.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 2: Nothing is applied yet: the title row pill still reads a green "Active".
  • Step 3: Before anything changes, a confirmation titled "Deactivate part?" opens on top of the part dialog.
  • Step 4: It is the application's standard confirmation: a title, message lines, a "Note (Optional)" field, "Cancel" and a red "Deactivate" button. There is no word to type to confirm.
  • Step 5: {Part-A} is still on the Active tab.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, v29 (14 Oct 2026 copy), S10-R1, S10-R2, S13-R21, read 14 Oct 2026; design canvas boards 3.2 (Inactive picked) and 3.3 (Save asks first), 13 Oct copy. Source-verified 14 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S10-R1: “A status change is confirmed before it is applied, from either entry point: the bulk bar (Stories 2 and 3), or Save in the part dialog after the user picks a different Part Status (S13-R21).”
  • S10-R2: “The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog. There is no confirmation word to type.”
  • S13-R21: “Picking a different status changes nothing until Save. When Save is pressed with a different status picked, the confirmation of Story 10 opens first.”
